Author: CrownedPandaXIV
Name: XIV Fleet Companion
Description:
Got a massive fleet of submarines? Always struggling to see which ones need upgrades? Wanna see your multi-account fleet at a glance? Give this a try!

Subs and their routes, supplies, parts, retainers, Free Companies, inventories, income, the market and trends, all in the game. Keep your fleet on this PC with nothing else to install, or share it between PCs (and with the free Windows app) through a database. Type /xivfleet to start.

Needs:
• AutoRetainer (from https://love.puni.sh/ment.json)

Works best with:
• Allagan Tools: bags, retainers' items and FC chests
• FC Tracker (from https://puni.sh/api/repository/erdelf): FC houses
• Submarine Tracker: voyage loot

Thanks to kawaii, NightmareXIV and the Puni.sh team (AutoRetainer), Critical_Impact (Allagan Tools), erdelf (FC Tracker) and Infi (Submarine Tracker) for their plugins.
Punchline: Here to help manage your EMPIAH!
Changelog:
Fixes from a full check of the plugin and the app. This entry grows until 2.5.0 is released.

- Restoring a shared-database backup works after an update that added fleet views. Before, any backup made before such an update failed to restore with a PostgreSQL message about CASCADE. The fleet views are now set aside first and made again straight after, whether the restore worked or not.
- After a restore or a move, every game writes all of its data again at its next sync. Before, data that hadn't changed since the plugin last wrote it was skipped for up to an hour, so a new, restored or moved database could show characters without their subs, retainers or bags until then. This also covers other games on the same PC and other PCs.
- Moving the fleet or restoring a backup waits for a running sync to finish, however long it takes. Before, it went ahead after a minute, while a big fleet's sync could still be writing.
- Voyage loot is no longer missed when subs are collected out of order. A sub that came back earlier but was collected after another sub's voyage was stored had its loot skipped for good. The plugin now keeps track per sub.
- A problem reading Submarine Tracker's file only affects the voyage loot. Before, it also stopped this PC's status (the app's PCs page) and venture rewards from saving. It's now listed as a problem on the PCs page.
- An FC chest is kept for a day when no character seems to be in that Free Company. AutoRetainer can briefly not know a character's Free Company, which used to remove the chest until the next hourly rewrite.
- Setup's administrator step reads its instructions as UTF-8 (a safeguard for Windows user names with accents).
- Two PCs with characters in one Free Company no longer swap its chest back and forth. Only the game whose character has the FC's subs writes the chest (any game does when nobody has subs there), so an old copy on another PC can't put back last month's chest, and the FC's salvage charts stop jumping.
- Allagan Tools is asked on the game's thread, as AutoRetainer is, so a sync can't catch it mid-change and report "open retainer X at a summoning bell" for no reason. If an Allagan Tools update changes how it answers, the plugin keeps the stored items (instead of reading them wrongly) and the PCs page says to update.
- FC Tracker's file that can't be read is now said on the PCs page (and logged once). Before, the house's last visit silently stopped updating until the 45-day demolition warning came up. An entry that looks blank (FC Tracker renamed something) is skipped, so a house isn't wiped from the app.
- A sync that only partly saved says so: the main window shows "Synced ... ago, partly" and, on hover, what wasn't saved. "Last sync" also updates when every character here is synced by another game.
- Plainer messages when the database is still starting up, has too many connections, is out of disk space, or the login isn't allowed to write; these are logged once, not every sync. An AutoRetainer update the plugin doesn't understand yet says to update XIV Fleet Companion, instead of showing an error.
- Two games on one PC with the same Account Label (or none) are told so, and to give each its own label: they share one row on the PCs page and overwrite each other's status.
- Which game a character last logged in on is now timed by the database's clock, so a PC whose clock is off can't lose (or win) a character wrongly.
- A renamed retainer's venture rewards aren't stored a second time under its new name.
- A retainer list AutoRetainer hasn't loaded yet (retainers with no id) is skipped rather than refused by the shared database every sync. A saved database login that can't be read is logged once and Settings says to enter it again.
- Updating or unloading the plugin mid-sync stops the sync and waits a moment for it, and settings are always saved on the game's thread.
- Restoring a shared-database backup pauses the plugins on your other PCs first, as moving the database does, so their syncs can't block it or write over it straight after.
- Backups use tools new enough for the database: an older PostgreSQL installed on the PC for something else is passed over for the downloaded tools, and when none are new enough it says so plainly.
- A failed daily backup tries again after 30 minutes, then longer, instead of every minute (each try started a process and wrote to the log). It's also made by the plugin when the app's daily task hasn't made one for two days.
- "Let other PCs connect" fixes a firewall rule left on another port (after setting PostgreSQL up again).
- Database updates have no time limit, but give way after 10 seconds when another PC is using a table, so they can't hold every other PC up.
- Moving the fleet from the shared database to this PC brings the shared database up to date first (an older one failed with a raw SQL error), and a move the other way can't end half-recorded.
- Moving or backing up works when the Windows user name or the database password has letters outside English: the copy goes to a folder the tools can open, and a refused password with such letters is said so.
- Removing a copy a move left behind names the PCs that may still need it to find the new address.
- The move window says to close the app on your other PCs first (a change made there during the move isn't copied). A damaged fleet file's advice also says to delete fleet.db-wal and fleet.db-shm.
- Income is much faster for a big fleet: on 80 characters with two months of history it took over two minutes; now about two seconds (the same answers).
- The shared database and the fleet file sort the same way: names and account labels go letter by letter whatever language the database PC's PostgreSQL was set up in, and missing names sort last on both.
- Windows of a number of days are exactly that many 24-hour days on both, so they don't shift by an hour after a daylight-saving change. The fleet file gets two more indexes (Trends for the whole fleet, the rank-up forecasts).
- A house warning now says "the game can demolish it in 3 more days" instead of "demolished after 3 more".
- Current gil/day picks the Fight Club row for the sub's own build (or, failing that, the fastest one its rank clears), not whichever row comes first in the spreadsheet, as the app now does.
- The Shopping List saves its checked ticks back, as the app does, so ticks for parts already crafted and held don't count again later when a new part is needed. A tick saved on two PCs at the same moment isn't lost.
- Not synced, with no account labels: characters are grouped by the PC they last logged in on, so closing one game no longer marks another game's characters as not synced. A character whose supplies aren't known yet isn't counted as low on them.
- Free Companies: an FC short on both rank and days says both ("Rank 2/6, and 25 more days").
- Market prices: the Shadow data centre is known, and Universalis's own list is asked again later if it couldn't be read at first.
- Route Optimization: with no sub off its Target route, it says why (no sub at rank 85 yet, or no Fight Club Data imported) instead of always "all on target", as the app now does.
- A chart that can't be read says why, instead of showing Loading for good and being read again and again (the fleet file busy, a dropped connection, no history yet).
- "Remove everything from this PC" keeps its result on screen (what was removed, or why it stopped), and the check of this PC no longer wipes other tools' results or restarts on its own.
- A Made number typed on the Shopping List is always saved, also when the list is worked out again under it. Unticking "all made" puts back the count from before, not 0.
- Saving a change says what went wrong: "Could not reach the database" only when it couldn't be reached.
- Test Database Connection connects the way syncing does (following a database that moved) and says a problem in plain words.
- Fight Club Data: a spreadsheet that can't be read says so, and merged cells are read right when the sheet doesn't start at A1 (in the app too).
- The Subs page's forecast line says when it couldn't be read. A passing database error no longer stops this PC's check-ins for the PCs page until the game restarts.
- Gil & Market: a fleet file without the loot view still shows the page (without loot prices).
- After the clocks go back, Inventory, Where Is It?, the Shopping List and Trends still refresh as usual.
- The unsold-days box follows a change made in the app or on another PC. Change order no longer flickers a row twice. Route Optimization shows a renamed character's new name. The "Choose characters" list is the right height at any UI scale. "Copied" on the Check page shows on the button, keeping the check's result. Supplies' "Updated" line sits on its own line. Database tools gives the last sync in local time with its offset, not marked UTC. Exported files are dated the same way as the app's on any calendar.
- Less work each frame on big fleets: Inventory (Characters, Fleet totals, Where Is It?), Retainers, Route Optimization, the sidebar and Summary work out their lists once per read, search or setting instead of every frame, and the colours are worked out once per look. Database tools reads the saved login and network adapters every few seconds, not every frame. Backups reads its settings every few seconds and lists the backup folder away from the game (a folder on a PC that's off no longer holds the game up), and looks for the app's backup task once at a time. The routes reuse the Parts read instead of reading the same views again.
- The same names as the app: Roster Name and Submarines, Venture type, FC name, Character override, the Parts Summary tab with Class needed and Still needed, Inventory's Character / FC / Fleet / Where Is It? tabs, and "World market / day". The Subs table has the app's columns in the app's order (Speed and Range shown), and sorts Current route by map first. "Another PC or account" instead of "another game"; Status's switch is called "Sync this game's fleet", as in Settings.
- Choosing a shared database puts the form for its details at the top of Settings, without the shared settings' read error above it.
- Loot per voyage: By route can be seen below a long subs table. "Ago" says days after 48 hours. Rank percent rounds exactly as the app. Sub Rules' All tick can be unticked (slot 1 stays). Market tables are the right height at any UI scale. The speed test's wording is up to date, and gives no frame time if the page wasn't open while it ran.
- Supplies has the app's "Ceruleum from FC Credits" section (the tanks each Free Company's credits buy and how long they last, per account and per FC, with the tank's price), and the app's summary: the fleet's use a day, what to buy to last the chosen days (with the repair kits' gil) and who runs out first. Days are worded as in the app ("6.2 days", "Under a day", "No use", "Not enough history").
- Income has the app's Difference / day column (real net less expected).
- High-quality items say "(HQ)". A high-quality stack is now stored as the game numbers it, so Inventory, Where Is It? and the Shopping List tell it apart (in the app too). Worn high-quality gear still counts for item level.
- Trends' history no longer grows for ever. Every change is kept; the hourly "still the same" repeats are thinned to one a day once they're over 30 days old, a week at a time in the background. No chart or figure changes.
- A database move that fails after every PC was sent to the new database keeps it (nothing is lost, and syncing carries on); only this PC's own saved details failing is reported.
- Releases are published only after the full tests pass.
